_comment: Keycloak type confusion campaign configuration for VALENCE fuzzer
_purpose: Run the same type confusion suite that found bugs in Vault, against Keycloak's OIDC token validation

identity_provider._comment: OIDC IdP pointing to mock-idp for token exchange

oidc_client._comment: Client in target realm for direct JWT validation testing

protocol_mappers._comment: Mappers to include groups and custom claims in tokens

roles_and_groups._comment: Keycloak realm roles and groups for group-based policy testing

campaign_config._comment: Engine configuration for JWTEngine when targeting Keycloak
campaign_config.role_name: N/A — Keycloak uses client scopes, not roles for JWT validation

authentication_methods._comment: How to submit tokens to Keycloak for validation

method_1_token_introspection._comment: Submit JWT to Keycloak's introspection endpoint — tests server-side validation

method_2_userinfo._comment: Submit JWT as Bearer token to userinfo endpoint — tests token acceptance

method_3_broker_token_exchange._comment: Exchange external IdP token through broker — tests claim mapping

manual_setup_steps: 1. Start Docker: cd docker && docker compose up -d && sleep 30
2. Wait for Keycloak to be ready: curl http://localhost:8080/realms/master (retry until 200)
3. Run docker/keycloak/setup.sh to create base realm (or use this config to create programmatically)
4. Create the 'valence-type-confusion' realm via Admin REST API
5. Create the OIDC IdP (mock-oidc-tc) — NOTE: uses Docker-internal hostname 'valence-mock-idp:9090'
6. Create the tc-test-client with protocol mappers for groups and department
7. Create roles, groups, and test user
8. IMPORTANT: Configure mock-idp to respond to Keycloak's OIDC discovery requests
9. Test baseline: obtain token via direct access grant, verify groups claim is present
10. Run campaign: use JWTEngine mutations, submit via token introspection endpoint

key_differences_from_vault.token_validation: Keycloak validates its OWN tokens (self-issued). For external token testing, use token exchange or broker flow.
key_differences_from_vault.groups_handling: Keycloak includes groups via protocol mapper. The groups claim format depends on the mapper config (full path vs short name).
key_differences_from_vault.claim_restrictions: Keycloak uses client scopes and audience restrictions, not bound_claims. The equivalent test is: does Keycloak accept a token with wrong audience in the 'aud' claim?
key_differences_from_vault.type_confusion_surface: Main attack surface is token exchange: submit an external JWT with type-confused claims and see if Keycloak maps them correctly to internal user attributes.
key_differences_from_vault.introspection_vs_login: Vault has a single login endpoint. Keycloak has introspection (checks token validity), userinfo (returns claims), and token exchange (swaps external token). Each may handle types differently.
